To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the interpolation operator can be implemented in a way that achieves 50% of peak performance for all polynomial degrees relevant in simulations, (2) the HelmholtZ operator can be implemented to achieve 50% of its peak performance for all degrees relevant in simulations and (3) the fast diagonalization method is capable of achieving 50% of performance for all degrees and can be implemented in an efficient way.

the performance of tensor product bases can be increased by 2 orders of magnitude compared to the state of the art, and that this performance is high enough to allow for the use of high order spectral element methods in industrial CFD applications.

the performance of the building block operators for spectral element methods is comparable to the performance of matrix matrix multiplication and that these operators are therefore not performance bottlenecks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
efficient implementations of the building block operators for CFD applications based on spectral element and discontinuous Galerin methods.
the development and implementation of a high performance spectral element method for CFD applications.
the efficient implementation of high order CFD methods, and the results obtained can be used to improve the performance of existing CFD solvers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tensor product bases are the best choice for CFD applications, if the implementation is done carefully.
the present implementation of the tensor product basis is a very good choice for high order spectral element and discontinuous Galero methods in computational fluid dynamics.
tensor product basis functions are the best choice for high order CFD applications, provided they are implemented in a suitable way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented methods are very fast and accurate.
we have developed a new, highly efficient, high order CFD method, which is able to solve complex problems in combustion and turbulence with a very small number of operations.
tensor product bases are a very efficient way to implement high order methods in the context of CFD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high performance of tensor product polynomial bases can be achieved without any special hardware support.
the high order methods can now be applied in production CFD codes without a significant runtime overhead.
high order methods are no longer restricted to small scale applications.
